Aperçu du poste : 
 Le spécialiste en analyse numérique a pour mission principale de renforcer notre stratégie et nos opérations d’analyse, tout en soutenant les initiatives de transformation numérique en cours chez Genetec. En tant que membre à part entière de l’équipe d’analyse, cette personne sera au cœur de nos processus d’analyse et de notre pile technologique, notamment Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Tag Manager (GTM), BigQuery, Data Studio, ainsi que des outils d’expérimentation ou d’analyse comportementale tels que les tests A/B et les cartes thermiques.  
 Le spécialiste contribuera au développement de nos pratiques d’analyse concernant le site web, le portail, la documentation technique, le commerce en ligne et le support technique, en surveillant les performances de nos principales propriétés numériques, en soutenant la mise en œuvre d’un suivi respectueux du consentement, en analysant les données, en validant leur exactitude et en créant des tableaux de bord pour les parties prenantes. En étroite collaboration avec d’autres équipes marketing internationales, ce poste permettra de traduire les objectifs commerciaux en résultats mesurables et d’orienter les décisions fondées sur les données et les informations pertinentes.  

 Qui êtes-vous ?  
 Vous êtes un(e) professionnel(le) de l’analyse soucieux(se) du détail qui apprécie de travailler concrètement sur la planification des mesures, la mise en œuvre du suivi, la validation des données, la création de rapports sur les ensembles de données et l’élaboration de tableaux de bord. Vous comprenez comment les données sont générées, structurées, nettoyées, validées, documentées et reliées entre les différentes plateformes, et vous adoptez une approche structurée et orientée vers les solutions pour transformer les questions métier en exigences mesurables et en informations pratiques.  

 Votre journée en un coup d'oeil :  
 Créer et maintenir des tableaux de bord et des ensembles de données évolutifs à l’aide de Looker Studio, BigQuery, SQL et des requêtes planifiées 
 Gérer et mettre en œuvre le cycle de vie des mesures pour les initiatives qui vous sont confiées, notamment la planification, la mise en œuvre, la validation, l’analyse, le reporting et le suivi 
 Maintenir et améliorer l’infrastructure analytique, notamment Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Tag Manager (GTM), DataLayer personnalisé, les ensembles de données BigQuery et les tableaux de bord Data Studio ; effectuer régulièrement des tests d’assurance qualité (QA) 
 Recueillir les exigences des parties prenantes en matière de reporting et de suivi, et traduire les besoins métier en indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) 
 Analyser et valider les données des plateformes d’analyse et de marketing afin de résoudre les problèmes, de rapprocher les rapports, de valider le suivi des conversions et de garantir la précision du suivi 
 Travailler avec les données provenant de Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn et Bing dans une optique de mesure et de suivi, et non d’exécution de campagnes 
 Comprendre comment les données issues des plateformes d’analyse et de marketing, des systèmes de gestion de contenu (CMS) et des systèmes de gestion de la relation client (CRM) interagissent tout au long du pipeline de mesure marketing de bout en bout, et valider les résultats analytiques par rapport aux systèmes sources connectés pertinents lorsque cela est nécessaire 
 Documenter la logique de suivi, les étapes de validation et les définitions de reporting, et partager les bonnes pratiques en matière d’analyse avec les parties prenantes du marketing 
 Collaborez avec les équipes marketing afin d’aligner l’analyse sur les performances des campagnes, l’expérience numérique et les objectifs commerciaux 
 Proposer des améliorations concernant le suivi, les processus de production de rapports et les pratiques en matière de qualité des données 

 Ce qui fait de vous un excellent candidat : 
 Diplôme universitaire en marketing numérique, en analyse de données ou dans un domaine connexe ; les certifications Google relatives à GA4 et BigQuery sont considérées comme un atout majeur 
 Au moins 5 ans d’expérience en analyse numérique/web dans un environnement de marketing numérique B2B 
 Solide expérience pratique de BigQuery, Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Tag Manager (GTM), de la mise en œuvre de couches de données personnalisées et de Data Studio 
 Expérience pratique de l’utilisation de BigQuery et du langage SQL pour l’analyse et la validation des données, y compris les jointures, les agrégations, l’exportation de données GA4 et les requêtes planifiées 
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de plans de mesure et la validation des données issues des plateformes d’analyse et de marketing ; excellente compréhension des événements, des conversions, de l’attribution, des données de performance et de la manière dont les ensembles de données s’articulent au sein du pipeline de mesure marketing 
 Connaissances pratiques de JavaScript pour le suivi, les événements personnalisés, les variables et les conditions de balisage 
 Compréhension de la manière dont les plateformes marketing telles que Google Ads, Meta, LinkedIn et Bing structurent les données, avec la capacité de connecter et de réconcilier des ensembles de données dans BigQuery 
 Solides compétences en communication ; capacité à traduire des conclusions techniques en informations métier claires et en recommandations pratiques 
 Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit (ce poste nécessite des interactions avec nos collaborateurs et clients internationaux) 

 Un atout si vous avez :  
 Expérience avec Power BI pour la visualisation avancée des données et la création de rapports 
 Connaissance des concepts, de la configuration, du dépannage ou de l'optimisation de Google Tag Manager côté serveur (sGTM)

job_title: Spécialiste, risques & prévention/Insider Risk & Data Loss Prevention Specialist
job_summary: Analyze insider-risk alerts, implement data-loss-prevention controls, and build risk and remediation dashboards. Candidates need three years in insider risk, incident response, data protection, or a related field. This full-time hybrid role advertises Montreal and requires French-English bilingualism.
job_responsibilities:
• Partner with our IT, Identity, Endpoint, Legal, HR, and Compliance teams to design practical controls that reduce insider risk in line with business priorities.
• Develop, implement, and maintain DLP and insider risk monitoring capabilities by translating scenarios into detection use cases, control requirements, response playbooks, and measurable risk indicators, with a focus on accidental data exposure, data exfiltration, policy violations, privilege misuse, and suspicious user behaviour.
• Configure and tune insider risk, DLP, and user activity monitoring controls using platforms such as Microsoft Purview, Sentinel, Defender for Endpoint, etc..
• Support the end-to-end lifecycle of insider risk investigations, including alert triage, analysis, documentation, and escalation of high-risk cases. Including collecting evidence, maintaining clear documentation, and supporting post-incident reviews.
• Develop dashboards, metrics, and reports that communicate insider risk trends, alert quality, control effectiveness, and remediation progress to security leadership.
• Help create awareness, guidance, and operational procedures that reduce accidental insider risk and promote secure handling of sensitive information.
experience_required:
3+ years of experience in data loss prevention, insider risk, incident response, threat detection, or a related field.
Practical understanding of SOC operations, alert triage, investigation workflows, escalation processes, and security incident documentation.
Experience with DLP, insider risk, endpoint detection, cloud security, or user activity monitoring tools.
Working knowledge of sensitive data protection concepts, including data classification, data handling, access governance, least privilege, and data exfiltration risks.
Ability to analyze logs, alerts, user behaviour, file activity, access patterns, and other telemetry to determine risk and recommend appropriate actions.
Strong judgment when handling sensitive investigations, confidential information, and employee-related risk cases.
Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Fluent in French and English, both verbal and written (this role requires interaction with our international collaborators and customers)
An asset if you have:
Hands-on experience with Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management and  Data Loss Prevention, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Entra ID, or related Microsoft security and compliance tools.
Ability to perform live-endpoint investigation: including the identification and gathering of key forensic artifacts, offline investigation and remediation actions as needed.
Experience developing detection rules, correlation searches, dashboards, playbooks, or investigation workflows in SIEM or SOAR platforms.
Understanding of role-based access control, audit logging, pseudonymization, and appropriate separation of duties in insider risk programs.
Familiarity with common insider risk scenarios, including accidental sharing, departing employee risk, unusual downloads, external sharing, use of personal cloud storage, removable media activity, and privilege misuse.
Knowledge of security frameworks, compliance requirements, or standards related to incident response, data protection, privacy, and information security.

La dynamique de votre équipe : 
 Genetec est à la recherche d’un(e) spécialiste des risques internes et de la prévention des pertes de données (DLP) pour rejoindre son équipe de sécurité de l’information.  

 Cette équipe travaille en étroite collaboration avec les équipes d’affaires et techniques afin de protéger Genetec, ses employés et ses clients contre les menaces internes et externes. Elle surveille les réseaux et les systèmes de l’entreprise, tout en assurant la protection des actifs grâce à l’identification, à l’analyse et à la gestion des incidents de sécurité potentiels.  

 Le ou la spécialiste des risques internes et de la prévention des pertes de données évoluera au sein du Centre des opérations de sécurité (SOC) et contribuera à réduire les risques liés aux activités internes malveillantes ou accidentelles au sein de l’organisation. Ce rôle collaborera avec les équipes de sécurité, TI, juridique, ressources humaines et conformité, ainsi qu’avec différents intervenants d’affaires, afin de concevoir, mettre en œuvre, surveiller et améliorer continuellement les contrôles de cybersécurité qui protègent les renseignements sensibles, la propriété intellectuelle et les systèmes d’affaires critiques.  

 Votre journée en un coup d'oeil :  
 Collaborer avec les équipes TI, de gestion des identités, de sécurité des postes de travail, juridiques, des ressources humaines et de conformité afin de concevoir des contrôles pratiques qui réduisent les risques internes tout en soutenant les priorités d’affaires.  
 Développer, mettre en œuvre et maintenir les capacités de prévention des pertes de données (DLP) et de surveillance des risques internes, en traduisant différents scénarios en cas d’usage en exigences de détection, exigences de contrôle, procédures d’intervention et indicateurs de risque mesurables, avec un accent sur l’exposition accidentelle de données, l’exfiltration de données, les violations de politiques, l’utilisation abusive de privilèges et les comportements utilisateurs suspects.  
 Configurer et optimiser les contrôles liés aux risques internes, à la DLP et à la surveillance de l’activité des utilisateurs à l’aide de plateformes telles que Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint et d’autres outils similaires.  
 Soutenir l’ensemble du cycle d’investigation des risques internes, incluant le triage des alertes, l’analyse, la documentation et l’escalade des cas à risque élevé. Cela comprend la collecte de preuves, la tenue d’une documentation rigoureuse et la participation aux analyses post-incident.  
 Développer des tableaux de bord, indicateurs et rapports permettant de communiquer les tendances relatives aux risques internes, la qualité des alertes, l’efficacité des contrôles, ainsi que l’avancement des mesures correctives auprès des responsables de la sécurité.  
 Contribuer à la création de programmes de sensibilisation, de lignes directrices et de procédures opérationnelles visant à réduire les risques internes accidentels et à promouvoir une gestion sécuritaire de l’information sensible.  

 Ce qui fait de vous un excellent candidat : 
 Minimum de 3 ans d’expérience en prévention des pertes de données (DLP), gestion des risques internes, réponse aux incidents, détection des menaces ou dans un domaine connexe.  
 Bonne compréhension des opérations d’un centre de sécurité opérationnel (SOC), incluant le triage des alertes, les processus d’enquête, les mécanismes d’escalade et la documentation des incidents de sécurité.  
 Expérience avec des solutions de DLP, de gestion des risques internes, de détection sur les postes de travail, de sécurité infonuagique ou de surveillance de l’activité des utilisateurs.  
 Connaissance des principes de protection des données sensibles, notamment la classification des données, leur gestion sécurisée, la gouvernance des accès, le principe du moindre privilège et les risques d’exfiltration de données.  
 Capacité à analyser des journaux, des alertes, des comportements des utilisateurs, des activités sur les fichiers, des modèles d’accès et d’autres données de télémétrie afin d’évaluer les risques et de recommander des actions appropriées.  
 Bon jugement dans la gestion d’enquêtes sensibles, d’informations confidentielles et de situations impliquant des employés.  
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication écrite et orale, avec la capacité de vulgariser des résultats techniques auprès d’auditoires techniques et non techniques.  
 Maîtrise du français et de l'anglais, tant à l'oral qu'à l'écrit (ce poste nécessite des interactions avec nos collaborateurs et clients internationaux) 

 Un atout si vous avez :  
 Expérience pratique avec Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management, Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Entra ID ou d’autres solutions de sécurité et de conformité de l’écosystème Microsoft.  
 Capacité à mener des investigations en direct sur les postes de travail, incluant l’identification et la collecte d’artefacts forensiques clés, ainsi que des activités d’analyse hors ligne et de remédiation, lorsque requises.  
 Expérience dans la création de règles de détection, de recherches de corrélation, de tableaux de bord, de procédures automatisées (playbooks) ou de processus d’enquête sur des plateformes SIEM ou SOAR.

full_job_post:
Customer Success Manager, Medical & Health Sciences Education
Vancouver, Canada; Calgary, Canada; Toronto, Canada; Halifax, Canada
Partner with the Higher Education Programs Preparing Tomorrow’s Healthcare Professionals.

The best customer relationships begin with trust: understanding what a partner is trying to achieve, helping them work through difficult challenges, and showing up with insight when it matters.

At Acuity Insights, those conversations happen in a uniquely meaningful context. We partner with medical and health sciences programs as they educate and develop the people who will become tomorrow’s healthcare professionals. Our Program Experience products help institutions manage complex academic programs, understand their data, and support learners throughout their journey.

As our next Customer Success Manager, you’ll build trusted partnerships with program leaders, educators, and administrators, helping them realize meaningful value from Acuity’s products while uncovering new opportunities to deepen those relationships over time.

This is a Customer Success role where helping customers realize long-term value naturally leads to renewals, growth, and lasting partnerships. Our strongest partnerships grow because customers trust our guidance, see meaningful outcomes, and choose to deepen their relationship with us over time.

You’ll also join at an important moment for our Customer Success team. We’re creating greater focus between Customer Success, Implementation, and Support so our CSMs can spend more of their time understanding their partners, strengthening relationships, driving value, and identifying opportunities for growth. The foundations are already here. You’ll have the opportunity to help shape what comes next.

If you enjoy becoming deeply invested in your customers’ success, developing a point of view about what will help them get there, and turning that understanding into trusted partnerships and meaningful growth, you’ll find a lot to dig into here.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in Canada.

Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is welcome. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

In your first few weeks, you’ll immerse yourself in our customers’ world. You’ll learn how medical and health sciences programs operate, get to know the institutions in your portfolio, and build your understanding of our Program Experience products: One45, Analytics, and MSPE Builder.

You’ll gradually take ownership of a focused portfolio of institutional partners, spanning a mix of mid-sized and strategic relationships. The portfolio is designed to give you the space to understand your customers deeply, build relationships across stakeholders, and take meaningful ownership of their success. You’ll have experienced teammates and specialized teams across Acuity to draw on as you build your product and domain expertise.

As you take ownership of your portfolio, you’ll:

Build relationships that go beyond the day-to-day.
Understand what matters to each partner, where they’re trying to go, and what may be getting in the way. You’ll work with programs ranging from established institutions with complex stakeholder environments to newer programs looking for more guidance.

Own the relationship, not every task.
Stay accountable for the partner and their outcomes while bringing in expertise from Implementation, Support, Product, Sales, and other teams when it’s needed.

Drive retention and uncover opportunities for growth.
Understand account health, anticipate risk, and identify where greater adoption or another Acuity solution could create meaningful value. When an opportunity is qualified, you’ll partner with Sales to move it forward.

Bring customer insight back into Acuity.
Look across your portfolio for patterns, challenges, and opportunities that can help Product, Sales, and other teams make better decisions.

Help shape how Customer Success works.
Look beyond your own portfolio for ways to improve how we manage customers, collaborate across teams, and use AI and other tools to make Customer Success more proactive and scalable.

Most of our Program Experience partners are in North America, with a significant concentration in the United States and a growing international footprint. Most of your work will happen remotely, with occasional opportunities to meet partners through campus visits, conferences, and industry events. 

What You’ll Help Make Possible

The relationships you build will have an impact far beyond your own portfolio. You’ll help medical and health sciences programs get more value from their partnership with Acuity while contributing directly to our growth.

Build partnerships customers want to grow.
Develop trusted, long-term relationships that help institutions achieve meaningful outcomes and continue choosing Acuity year after year.

Help customers solve bigger challenges.
Understand what your partners are trying to accomplish and develop a point of view about how Acuity can help. Connect them with the products, insights, and expertise that move them toward their goals rather than simply responding to the request in front of you.

Spot opportunities to create more value.
Help partners get greater value from the solutions they use today and identify where other Acuity capabilities could help them solve new problems.

Bring the voice of the customer into Acuity.
Turn what you’re hearing across your portfolio into insight that can inform better products, stronger customer experiences, and smarter business decisions.

Help define the next chapter of Customer Success.
Contribute ideas and improve how the team works together as we build a more strategic, commercially accountable, and customer-centered CS function.

The impact of your work will be visible in stronger customer relationships, healthier renewals, meaningful commercial growth, and institutions that continue choosing Acuity as a trusted partner. Behind those outcomes are medical and health sciences programs preparing people for careers that have a profound impact on the communities they serve.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role isn’t about quick wins. It’s about earning trust, developing judgment, creating momentum, and delivering meaningful outcomes for both your customers and the business.

In your first few months, you’ll build your understanding of our products, customers, and the medical and health sciences education environment while beginning to take ownership of customer relationships. There’s meaningful domain and product knowledge to learn, and you’ll have support from experienced teammates as you build confidence.

As you ramp, you’ll establish strong relationships across your accounts and develop healthy rhythms around customer engagement, renewal readiness, account health, and portfolio planning. You’ll increasingly know when to advise directly and when bringing in specialized expertise will create a better customer outcome.

By the end of your first year, you’ll be a trusted advisor to your customers, confidently leading strategic conversations and contributing directly to retention and revenue growth. Your customers will know they can count on you, and your teammates will value the perspective and insight you bring back from your portfolio.

Who You’ll Work With

You’ll report to our Senior Manager, Customer Success (Program Experience), joining a close-knit team with deep knowledge of our customers, products, and the medical and health sciences environment.

Customer Success is deeply collaborative at Acuity. You’ll maintain ownership of the partner relationship while working closely with specialized teams across the business:

Implementation, who lead onboarding, configuration, and implementation while you maintain customer context and relationship continuity.

Support, who provide specialized issue resolution while you stay connected to anything affecting the health of the relationship.

Sales, to align on account strategy, renewals, and qualified growth opportunities.

Product, to bring customer challenges, patterns, and context into product conversations.

Some of your biggest contributions will come from connecting the dots: understanding what matters to the customer, bringing the right people together, and helping Acuity see patterns and opportunities beyond a single account.

How You’ll Succeed Here

There’s no single profile for success in this role. But the people who thrive here tend to be curious, thoughtful, strategically minded, and genuinely invested in helping their customers succeed.

You stay curious.
You want to understand the problems your customers are trying to solve, not just the products they use. You ask thoughtful questions, connect the dots, and look beyond the immediate request to understand what matters most. When you spot a problem, you think about what could solve it, and whether there’s something others could learn from it too.

You build expertise.
You enjoy learning. Whether it’s our products, medical and health sciences education, or the higher education landscape, you know the best customer conversations are grounded in deep understanding.

You take ownership.
You see your portfolio as something you own, not something you manage. When something is unclear or evolving, you move work forward, follow through, and stay engaged until there’s a clear outcome.

You communicate with clarity and confidence.
You’re thoughtful, direct, and comfortable having difficult conversations when needed. You create clarity, build trust, and help people move forward together.

You thrive in change.
You’re comfortable in an evolving environment, adapt when priorities shift, and use new tools, including AI, thoughtfully to work more effectively and better support your customers.

You balance customer success with commercial thinking.
You understand that strong customer relationships and strong business outcomes go hand in hand. You’re comfortable leading renewal conversations, identifying growth opportunities, and helping customers invest where they’ll see genuine value.

Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running

There’s no single path into this role, and we don’t believe great Customer Success talent is measured by years of experience alone. What matters most is that you’ve built customer relationships, taken ownership of outcomes, and learned from those experiences.

You’ll likely bring experience in:

Customer Success, account management, consulting, or another customer-facing role where you’ve independently owned customer relationships or a portfolio.

Building trusted relationships across multiple stakeholders in complex customer organizations.

Supporting customer adoption, retention, and renewals while balancing customer value with business outcomes.

Identifying customer needs and opportunities where additional products, services, or expertise could create value.

Navigating challenging conversations and ambiguity with sound judgment and confidence.

Using CRM or Customer Success platforms such as Salesforce, ChurnZero, or similar tools.

Working independently in a remote environment with a high degree of ownership and initiative.

Supporting customers across North American time zones.

Experience in higher education, healthcare education, or complex B2B SaaS environments may help you ramp more quickly, but it isn’t required. We care more about your ability to learn, build trust, think critically, and take ownership.

If you’re earlier in your Customer Success career but have demonstrated exceptional curiosity, ownership, and a track record of building trusted customer relationships, we’d still love to hear from you.

How We Support You

Transparent compensation. A base salary between $78,000 - $85,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.

Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening technical skills, building confidence, or exploring new areas of interest.

Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.

Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.

Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.

Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.

Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.

We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some of our conversations, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.

Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you. 

Steps in the Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision. 

Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.

Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.

Hiring Manager Conversation. A conversation about how you build trusted customer relationships, navigate ambiguity, and balance customer outcomes with commercial success. You’ll also have the opportunity to learn more about the evolution of Customer Success at Acuity, the portfolio you’ll support, and the challenges we’re working to solve alongside our partners.

Team Conversations. You’ll meet members of our Customer Success and Growth Enablement & Execution teams to explore how we work together across the customer journey. It’s also an opportunity for you to ask questions, get to know future teammates, and see what it would be like to work together day to day.

Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.

Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 130+ people who care deeply about our work and about each other. We want Acuity to be a place where people can do meaningful work, have room to grow, and build careers that are sustainable over time.

We put a lot of trust in people to own their work, make good decisions, and manage their time in ways that work for them and their teams. Being remote means we’re thoughtful about how we communicate and collaborate, creating space for focused work while making time to connect when it matters.

Day to day, that looks like:

High trust and autonomy in how work gets done

Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team

Space for deep work, balanced with intentional moments of connection

Curiosity, care, and people who are willing to help each other

That approach has earned Acuity recognition as one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers, an award that considers workplace culture, employee wellness, and people practices.

As Acuity grows and changes, we keep paying attention to how it feels to work here and making deliberate choices to protect what works while continuing to make it better.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights grew out of two separate challenges inside Canadian medical education.

One45 began at the University of British Columbia in the early 2000s, where educators were looking for a better way to manage the complex work of medical training. A few years later at McMaster University, researchers began exploring how admissions teams could understand more about applicants than grades and test scores alone. That work became Casper.

Those two paths came together in 2021. Today, Acuity builds products that support higher education institutions across more of the learner journey, from admissions and assessment through to program management, insight, and learner development.

Our work is still grounded in the same approach that shaped those early beginnings: start with a real problem, understand it deeply, and use research and technology thoughtfully to build something better.

Today, we continue to modernize our products, invest in research and innovation, and explore new ways to help institutions better understand and support human potential.

Senior Admissions Test Content Specialist (Casper) - English & French
Montreal, Canada; Ottawa, Canada; Toronto, Canada
Help shape how human potential is understood.

If you’re the kind of person who enjoys untangling complexity, spotting subtle patterns, and asking thoughtful questions before settling on an answer, this might be the role you’ve been looking for.

Traditional admissions measures do a good job of assessing academic achievement, but they don’t tell the whole story. People are more than their grades. Human skills like empathy, ethics, communication, resilience, and collaboration matter too, especially for the professionals our communities rely on every day.

Casper helps higher education programs better understand applicants’ human skills, giving them a more complete picture of each person’s potential.

As a Senior Admissions Test Content Specialist, you’ll play an important role in making that possible. Working alongside researchers, assessment specialists, and fellow content experts, you’ll help build the assessments that applicants complete and institutions rely on to make admissions decisions. You’ll use language, critical thinking, and judgment to ensure every assessment is clear, balanced, fair, and ready for use in high-stakes admissions decisions.

Beyond writing and reviewing assessment content, you’ll own recurring content workflows that keep our assessments accurate, consistent, and ready for use. You’ll coordinate review cycles, bring together perspectives from multiple contributors, and make decisions that balance evidence, quality, and fairness.

This isn’t traditional content writing. It’s collaborative work that blends language, analytical thinking, and sound judgment to build assessments that help people be understood more completely.

This role requires professional fluency in English and French. English is the primary language of collaboration across Acuity, while French is used as part of the assessment content you’ll help build and review.

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in Canada.

Before you apply: Thoughtful use of AI is encouraged. If you use it to support your application, make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. The strongest applications are authentic, original, and unmistakably yours.

The Work You’ll Do

Every Casper assessment is carefully assembled from a large library of scenarios, questions, and supporting content. Building an assessment isn’t simply a matter of selecting questions. It requires hundreds of thoughtful decisions to ensure the final assessment is balanced, fair, and measures the human skills it’s designed to assess.

That’s where you’ll come in.

Working alongside experienced teammates, researchers, and reviewers, you’ll help transform individual pieces of content into complete admissions assessments. You’ll evaluate language, identify inconsistencies, balance competing considerations, and think carefully about how each decision shapes both the applicant experience and the quality of the assessment.

Some days you’ll refine wording to remove ambiguity. Other days you’ll review how scenarios work together across an entire assessment, identify gaps, improve supporting resources, or prepare new content for future test cycles.

No two days look exactly alike, but almost every day involves asking thoughtful questions, weighing trade-offs, and making decisions where nuance matters.

As Casper continues to grow, you’ll also help improve how we build assessments by exploring new tools, including AI, that allow us to scale without compromising the quality, fairness, and care applicants and institutions expect.

In your first few months, you’ll:

Learn how Casper assessments are designed, compiled, and reviewed alongside experienced teammates.

Build confidence contributing to live assessment cycles while developing an understanding of the frameworks that guide our decisions.

Learn how we evaluate clarity, fairness, balance, and validity across an entire assessment.

Begin contributing ideas and asking questions that strengthen both our content and the processes behind it.

As you grow, you’ll:

Compile complete Casper assessments in partnership with a reviewer, balancing content, timing, and assessment objectives.

Refine language and structure so every scenario and question is clear, consistent, and accessible.

Apply thoughtful judgment when categorizing scenarios and connecting them to the human skills they measure.

Help steward the quality of our assessment content by coordinating recurring review workflows, bringing together perspectives from colleagues and subject matter experts, and ensuring supporting materials are accurate, consistent, and ready for use.

Develop and refine supporting content and documentation that strengthens the quality, consistency, and integrity of our assessments.

Explore opportunities to improve how we work, including using AI to streamline repetitive tasks while preserving the human judgment that underpins our assessments.

Collaborate with researchers, writers, reviewers, and production specialists to continuously improve how Casper is built.

What You’ll Help Make Possible

The work you do won’t just shape individual assessments. It will influence how applicants experience Casper, how institutions make admissions decisions, and how we continue to improve the way we build assessments.

Build assessments people trust. Create assessments that are clear, balanced, fair, and grounded in research.

Strengthen how we work. Improve the tools, processes, and ways of working that help us grow without compromising the quality applicants and institutions expect.

Advance the craft of assessment development. Contribute ideas that improve how we compile, review, and continuously refine Casper assessments.

Shape what’s next. Help thoughtfully incorporate new technologies, including AI, while preserving human judgment at the heart of our work.

Every improvement you make, whether it’s refining a single question or strengthening an assessment process, contributes to something much bigger: helping people be understood more completely.

What Success Looks Like

Success in this role isn’t about mastering everything right away. It’s about steadily building the judgment, confidence, and context to make thoughtful decisions that strengthen every assessment you contribute to.

In your first few months, success looks like:

Building a strong understanding of how Casper assessments are designed, compiled, and reviewed.

Applying careful attention to language, structure, and detail while learning when to ask questions and when to trust your judgment.

Identifying inconsistencies, raising thoughtful questions, and looking beyond the obvious answer.

Welcoming feedback as an essential part of the work, using it to strengthen both your thinking and the assessments you help build.

Becoming a dependable teammate who contributes consistently and helps keep assessment development moving forward.

As you grow, success means:

Confidently compiling and reviewing assessments with increasing independence.

Recognizing patterns, connections, and potential issues before they become problems.

Exercising sound judgment to balance clarity, fairness, validity, and the overall applicant experience.

Contributing ideas that improve how Casper assessments are built, whether through better processes, clearer content, or thoughtful use of AI.

Becoming a trusted thought partner whose perspective strengthens both our assessments and the way we work.

Over time, you’ll develop something that’s difficult to teach but invaluable to the team: the judgment to recognize subtle issues, ask the right questions, and make thoughtful decisions that strengthen both our assessments and the experience of the people who take them.

Who You’ll Work With

You’ll join Acuity’s Assessment Content Team, the group responsible for bringing Casper to life, from developing new scenarios to building the final assessments applicants complete.

The work is highly collaborative. Questions are encouraged, feedback is part of everyday work, and it’s common for teammates to think through difficult decisions together. Some of the best ideas begin with, “I’m not sure about this…” or “Can I get another perspective?”

Everyone reviews work, and everyone’s work is reviewed. That’s intentional. It’s how we learn from one another, strengthen our thinking, and ensure every assessment meets the high standards applicants and institutions expect.

You’ll work most closely with teammates who specialize in assessment compilation and review, learning from their experience as you build your own judgment and expertise. Along the way, you’ll also collaborate with:

Scenario developers and production specialists, who create the scenarios and video content that form the foundation of every Casper assessment.

Researchers and psychometricians, who help ensure our assessments are valid, reliable, and measure the human skills they’re designed to assess.

Operations and enablement partners, who coordinate assessment delivery, improve processes, and support the systems behind our work.

As you grow in the role, you’ll become an important contributor to the conversations that shape how Casper evolves, not just through the assessments you help build, but through the ideas, questions, and perspectives you bring to the team.

What You Bring to the Table

There’s no single career path that leads here.

Some of our team members came from education. Others from curriculum development, editing, assessment, instructional design, content development, or research. What they have in common isn’t a specific job title. It’s the way they approach complex work and the judgment they bring to it. They enjoy untangling difficult questions, looking at problems from different angles, and arriving at well-reasoned decisions.

If you’re excited by the opportunity to help shape how human potential is understood, here’s what we’ve found helps people thrive on this team.

Experience Working with Language.
You’ve built strong written communication skills through professional experience where language mattered. That might have been through teaching, curriculum development, instructional design, assessment, editing, academic publishing, content development, communications, or another role where precision, clarity, and consistency were essential.

You know language isn’t just about sounding good. It’s about communicating ideas clearly and minimizing ambiguity.

Professional Fluency in English and French.
You have professional written fluency in both English and French and enjoy working carefully with language in both. You’re able to recognize nuance, refine wording, and make sound editorial decisions while preserving meaning and intent across each language.

Making Thoughtful Decisions.
You’ve worked in an environment where judgment mattered.

You’re experienced at weighing competing considerations, applying frameworks or guidelines consistently, and making careful decisions where there isn’t always a single obvious answer. You understand that small decisions can have meaningful downstream consequences, and you enjoy thinking through those trade-offs.

Delivering High-Quality, Detail-Oriented Work.
You’ve managed work where accuracy and consistency couldn’t be left to chance.

Whether reviewing complex documents, developing educational materials, editing content, conducting quality assurance, or coordinating detailed projects, you’ve demonstrated the ability to produce reliable, high-quality work while balancing competing priorities and recurring responsibilities.

AI Is Already Part of How You Work.
AI isn’t something you’re curious about trying someday. It’s already part of your day-to-day workflow.

Whether you use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, or other AI tools, you’re already using them to research, organize information, explore ideas, improve writing, or reduce repetitive work. More importantly, you’ve developed the judgment to know when AI is helping, when it needs direction, and when human thinking needs to lead.

You enjoy exploring new technology, experimenting with better ways of working, and thoughtfully incorporating AI where it genuinely improves the quality of your work.

How You Approach Work

Experience will help you get started. The way you think will determine how successful you become.

Thoughtful Judgment.
You enjoy working through complex questions where there isn’t always a single right answer. You’re energized by nuance, curious enough to explore different perspectives, and thoughtful enough to resist jumping to easy conclusions. You know when to slow down, ask good questions, and think through the implications before moving forward.

Curiosity.
You naturally investigate inconsistencies, look for patterns, and enjoy understanding why something works before deciding how it could work better. You find satisfaction in uncovering insights, solving complex problems, and continually learning.

Perspective-Taking.
You’re able to step into someone else’s shoes, anticipating how different people might interpret language, experience a scenario, or respond to an assessment. You understand that strong assessment development starts with understanding the people it’s designed for.

Collaboration & Feedback.
You enjoy discussing ideas, giving and receiving feedback, and improving your thinking through conversations with others. You see review as an opportunity to strengthen both the work and the people behind it.

Organization & Reliability.
You’re able to manage recurring work, balance multiple priorities, and consistently follow through on commitments. People know they can count on you to deliver consistently high-quality work.

Adaptability.
You enjoy learning, evolving, and improving the way you work. As priorities shift, processes change, and new challenges emerge, you’re quick to adapt, open to new ideas, and motivated by finding better ways to move forward.

A Diversity of Perspectives Makes Us Stronger

We know there are many ways to develop the skills this role requires, and we know great candidates don’t always meet every bullet point in a job posting.

If your experience looks a little different but you believe your judgment, curiosity, and approach to solving complex problems would help you succeed here, we’d encourage you to apply.

We also know that better assessments are built by teams with diverse perspectives and lived experiences. Whether that’s through your cultural background, language skills, professional experience, or the unique perspective you bring to your work, we’d love to learn more about what you could add to our team.

How We Support You

Transparent compensation. The starting salary for Senior roles is between $75,000 - $85,000 CAD. Final offers reflect experience, scope, market alignment, and internal equity.

Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, whether that’s deepening technical skills, building confidence, or exploring new areas of interest.

Shared success. Access to employee stock options, so you share in the value you help create.

Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.

Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.

Future-focused support. A 2% GRSP matching program to help you plan ahead.

Support for growing families. A 16-week parental leave top-up beyond EI, available to all parents.

What Happens After You Apply

We review every application carefully. Whether you apply directly, are referred, or connect through a recruiter or hiring manager, you’ll receive equal consideration.

We don’t use AI to evaluate applications, though you may be automatically screened out if you don’t meet baseline requirements (e.g. Canadian residency and valid work authorization). In some interviews, AI may help with note-taking, but all evaluations and decisions are made by real humans.

Our interviews are two-way conversations. We want to understand your career, abilities, and goals, and help you assess whether this opportunity and team are the right fit for you. 

Steps in the Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks from initial conversation to final decision. 

Application Review. A real person reviews your application for potential fit.

Intro Conversation. A conversation with a member of our Talent team to learn about your career journey, what you’re looking for next, and to introduce you to Acuity, Casper, and the role.

Hiring Manager Conversation. A conversation focused on how you approach complex work, make thoughtful decisions, and collaborate with others. You’ll also have the opportunity to learn more about the role, the team, and the challenges we’re solving.

Assessment Exercise. We’ll ask you to work through an exercise that reflects the kind of thinking this role requires. We want to understand how you approach a complex question, explore it from different angles, use judgment to make decisions, and communicate your thinking. The exercise will also give you a chance to show how you use technology to support your work.

Team Conversations. You’ll meet members of the Content Team to explore how we work together, discuss real examples of collaboration and feedback, and give both you and the team the opportunity to see what it would be like to work together.

Decision. The hiring manager reviews feedback from the interview team and typically makes a decision within 2 to 4 business days.

Offer & Reference Checks. If it’s a match, we’ll move to references and a formal offer.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people who care deeply about our work and about each other.

Our culture is intentionally designed. As we’ve grown, we’ve made deliberate choices about how we work together, prioritizing trust, flexibility, and a sustainable pace so people can do meaningful work over the long term.

That commitment has been recognized externally. Acuity Insights has been named one of Canada’s Top Small & Medium Employers for the second consecutive year, reflecting our focus on building a strong, people-first environment.

Day to day, that shows up in how we collaborate:

High trust and autonomy in how work gets done

Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team

Space for deep work, balanced with intentional moments of connection

A culture grounded in care, curiosity, and shared purpose

As we continue to grow, we’re focused on maintaining that balance, building a company where people can do their best work and grow over time, without losing what makes the environment feel human.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.

Our work is grounded in a simple idea: that people are more than their grades, and that potential can be understood and developed, not just measured.

Our Casper situational judgment test (SJT), created by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is one of the most widely used open-response SJTs in higher education, backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we are evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions not just identify potential, but actively support its growth over time. As part of that evolution, we’re increasingly building toward a more connected ecosystem across assessment, education, and learner development. While teams remain focused on their individual products, we’re creating stronger connections across our platform to deliver more cohesive experiences for institutions and learners.

Senior Growth Marketing Manager
Toronto, Canada
Build the demand engine for Acuity’s next stage of growth.

Acuity Insights is entering a new stage of growth. We’ve spent years building products used by higher education programs to make important decisions about who enters their programs and how learners are supported once they get there. Today, established products are evolving, newer products are being commercialized, and we’re exploring how to reach new audiences and markets.

As our Senior Growth Marketing Manager, you’ll help turn that opportunity into demand.

You’re not walking into a blank slate, and you’re not inheriting a finished playbook. You’ll have enough foundation to move quickly and enough room to bring your own experience, ideas, and point of view to what comes next.

You’ll have working campaigns, a strong webinar program, recurring prospect communications, established cross-functional partners, and improving data and measurement capabilities to build from.

You’ll also have real whitespace. Nurture is a capability we need to build. International demand generation is largely unexplored. And we want you to bring the AI practices you’re already using in Growth Marketing to help accelerate our adoption, from campaign development and content repurposing to research, testing, and analysis. Across all of it, we want to get much better at understanding what creates qualified pipeline and contributes to revenue.

You’ll be our only dedicated Growth Marketer, working hands-on across strategy and execution while surrounded by partners across Marketing and our broader Growth organization. This opportunity will suit you particularly well if you like getting close to the business, figuring out where marketing can have the greatest commercial impact, and turning that judgment into action.

Before you apply: This is full-time, 16-month fixed-term employment covering an upcoming parental leave, open to candidates based anywhere in Canada.  The start date is early November 2026. You’ll work remotely within Canada with access to employee benefits including healthcare coverage, paid time off, and a learning and development budget.

Thoughtful use of AI is welcome. If you use it to support your application, please make sure it helps communicate your experience clearly and accurately. Authenticity and originality will help you stand out.

The Work You’ll Do

You’ll start with Acuity’s company-wide onboarding program, building context on our business, products, customers, and how we work. From there, you’ll go deeper into Marketing and our broader Growth organization, getting close to the campaigns, data, priorities, relationships, and rhythms that shape Growth Marketing today.

As you ramp, you’ll take increasing ownership of demand generation across our product portfolio, with the context and relationships you need to make good decisions and move independently.

Take ownership of demand generation

You’ll set and run our quarterly demand-generation plans, deciding how Growth Marketing can best contribute to our commercial priorities and where to focus across competing opportunities.

That means moving comfortably between strategy and execution: identifying the audiences and opportunities worth pursuing, choosing the right channels and tactics, building and launching the work, measuring what happens, and using what you learn to decide what comes next.

You’ll have autonomy to bring your own judgment and experience to the work, while staying closely connected to the business priorities, product developments, and customer insights that should shape it.

Turn product momentum into demand

You’ll work across a portfolio at different stages of maturity. Casper and One45 are established products with deep roots in higher education, with One45 now evolving into  its next chapter. Video Interviews and Professional Skills Development are newer solutions  we’re actively commercializing.

Working with Product Marketing, Sales, Customer Success and Business Development, you’ll translate product positioning, market insight, customer needs, and commercialization priorities into demand-generation strategies that reach the right audiences and give them a reason to engage.

You’ll gather context, develop a point of view about how Growth Marketing can contribute, recommend an approach, and carry it into market.

Build demand across the funnel

You’ll architect, execute, and optimize integrated campaigns across the channels that make sense for the audience and opportunity, including paid media, email, web, content, prospect communications, and new approaches worth testing.

You’ll continue building on a webinar program that has shown strong potential for generating qualified demand, owning the Growth Marketing motion end-to-end from audience and promotion strategy through registration, follow-up, and measurement.

And you’ll build and evolve nurture programs beyond their current state: developing more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, identifying useful triggers and segmentation, and creating paths that help accelerate leads  toward sales readiness.

Get closer to what actually drives growth

You’ll help us become much more disciplined about asking: What worked? What generated qualified demand? What progressed into pipeline? What contributed to revenue? And what should we do differently next time?

Using HubSpot, campaign data, and our evolving business intelligence capabilities, you’ll look beyond surface-level engagement metrics to understand how Growth Marketing contributes further down the funnel.

You’ll establish stronger measurement rhythms, test targeting and messaging, compare performance across campaigns and channels, and use what you learn to make better decisions about where we invest our time and budget.

You won’t control every downstream revenue outcome, but you’ll understand the connection between your work and the commercial funnel and take accountability for continuously improving that contribution.

Put AI to work in Growth Marketing

You’ll bring AI practices that are already part of your toolkit and help us apply them meaningfully at Acuity. That could include campaign development, research, content creation and repurposing, nurture, experimentation, and analysis, as well as use cases we haven’t identified yet.

The goal isn’t AI for its own sake. It’s finding practical ways to reduce manual work, get more leverage from what we create, improve quality and speed, and make better decisions. When something works, you’ll help turn it into a practice the broader team can learn from and continue using.

Test how we generate demand internationally

As Acuity expands its international reach, you’ll help us learn how our demand-generation approach translates into priority market including  Australia and New Zealand (ANZ), UK and Ireland.

Working with partners across Growth, you’ll develop and run a focused demand-generation pilot in one of these markets. You’ll help determine the audience, messaging, channels, and measures of success, then use what happens in this market to build an evidence-based point of view about what we should test, change, or invest in next.

Who You’ll Work With, and How

You’ll report to our Director of Marketing and join a Marketing function that includes Marketing Operations, Digital Marketing, Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Content and Communications.

You’ll be our dedicated Growth Marketing expert. That means bringing your own expertise while knowing how to draw on the expertise around you.

Sales and Business Development will be particularly important partners. They’re close to prospective customers every day and can help you understand the problems buyers are talking about, the language they use, what resonates, where opportunities are stalling, and what they’re hearing in the higher education market.

You’ll collaborate with Customer Success to dig deeper into buyer insights, source speakers for virtual events, understand expansion opportunities, and amplify post-event follow-up.

Your job is to listen closely, connect those insights with what you know about demand generation, and turn them into a point of view and a plan. Collaboration here doesn’t mean waiting for consensus or for someone else to tell you what campaign to run.

You’ll work closely with Product Marketing to understand positioning, value propositions, audiences, and product messaging, then translate that foundation into campaigns and experiences designed for the people we want to reach.

Within Marketing, you’ll collaborate with Customer Marketing, Events Marketing, Communications, Marketing Operations, and Creative teams  to bring campaigns, customer proof points, thought leadership, webinars, and other experiences to life.  

And with RevOps, you’ll strengthen the connection between marketing activity, lead progression, pipeline, and revenue so what we learn can shape what we do next.

You won’t need to know everything yourself. You will need to know your craft, build strong relationships, ask good questions, make recommendations, and keep things moving.

The Impact You’ll Have

Over the course of your time with us, you’ll help build a stronger and more scalable demand-generation engine. Your impact will show up in:

Greater commercial accountability. We’ll have clearer visibility into which campaigns, channels, audiences, and messages are creating qualified demand, progressing into pipeline, and contributing to revenue.

A stronger nurture capability. We’ll have more intentional journeys for different audiences and verticals, giving promising demand more opportunities to progress toward sales readiness.

Stronger commercialization. Professional Skills Development, Video Interviews, and the continued evolution of One45 will have focused demand-generation strategies supporting their growth in market.

A more connected event-to-demand engine. Webinars and virtual events will connect more intentionally to follow-up, nurture, pipeline progression, and what we learn from each program.

AI practices that create real leverage. We’ll have practical, proven ways of using AI to improve how Growth Marketing researches, creates, experiments, analyzes, and gets more from the work we produce.

Evidence to inform international growth. We’ll have real market learnings from demand-generation experimentation in a priority international market, giving us a stronger foundation for what to test or invest in next.

Across all of it, you’ll help us make growth decisions with more evidence and confidence, while leaving the demand engine stronger than you found it.

How You’ll Succeed Here

There’s no single profile for success in this role. But the person who thrives here will probably recognize themselves in a few things.

You think commercially.
Campaign activity is interesting to you because of what happens next. You want to understand whether people engaged, whether they became qualified opportunities, whether pipeline moved, and what that tells you about where to invest next.

You bring a point of view.
You listen to Sales, Business Development, Product, customer insights, market data,, but you don’t need everyone else to design the answer for you. You synthesize what you’ve learned, make recommendations, and move the work forward proactively.

You know how to create momentum with what you have.
You don’t need a huge budget, a large team, or a perfectly established playbook before you can make progress. You’re resourceful about figuring out what matters most, where to focus, and what you can build, test, or improve with the resources around you.

You’re genuinely hands-on.
You move fluidly between planning and doing, comfortably zooming out to set campaign strategy or diving into an ad platform, webinar plan, landing page, or email flow to make it real. You don't need a large team around you to move work forward.  You can inherit something that already works, respect what has been built, and still see where it could become better.

You experiment with purpose.
You’re willing to try something new, but experimentation isn’t throwing ideas at a wall. You start with a hypothesis, look at what happened, learn from it, and decide whether to iterate, scale, or stop.

You use AI as part of your craft.
You’ve moved beyond simply being curious about AI. You’re already using it in your work, learning where it creates leverage, where human judgment matters, and how it can help you move faster or produce better work.

You’re comfortable making choices.
You've worked in environments where priorities evolve and the playbook isn't always complete. You bring structure, judgment, and a bias toward action while staying focused on measurable business impact.  

Experience That Will Help You Hit the Ground Running

We care more about what you’ve actually owned, built, learned, and improved.

You’ll likely bring experience:

Owning B2B demand generation with accountability for qualified leads, pipeline, and commercial outcomes, ideally in SaaS or another complex B2B environment.

Personally designing, launching, measuring, and optimizing integrated campaigns across channels such as paid media, email, web, content, nurture, and virtual events.

Bringing a new product or meaningful product development to market and building demand around it.

Independently planning and executing webinars or other virtual events end to end, including content strategy, speaker sourcing, promotion, event flow, live execution, and post-event follow-up.

Using marketing and funnel data to evaluate performance, identify patterns, make investment decisions, and understand how marketing activity contributes to pipeline and revenue.

Building or significantly improving nurture programs, segmentation, automation flows, and recurring prospect communications using HubSpot or similar platforms.

Partnering closely with Sales and Product Marketing to turn customer, market, and product insight into effective demand-generation strategies.

Using AI meaningfully in your day-to-day marketing work to improve the quality, speed, analysis, or scale of what you produce.

Experience generating demand outside North America, particularly in Australia/New Zealand or the UK/Ireland, would be valuable as we begin testing our approach in these markets.

And if you’ve previously been the only Growth Marketer, or one of very few, you’ll bring particularly relevant experience for the level of ownership this role offers.

How We Support You

Transparent compensation. A salary between $110,000–$135,000 CAD, aligned to role scope, experience, and internal equity.

Learning that grows with you. A $3,000 annual learning budget to invest in your development, to deepen your expertise, build new skills, or explore new areas of interest.

Remote-first work. Fully remote within Canada, with up to six weeks per year to work internationally.

Time to rest and reset. Self-directed vacation (most teammates take 4–6 weeks annually), monthly Acuity Days (a collective Friday off), plus a two-week company-wide closure each December.

Comprehensive care. Health benefits from day one for you and your dependents.

What Happens After You Apply

Application Review. A member of our Talent team reviews your application.

Intro Conversation. You’ll meet with a member of our Talent team to explore your experience, what you’re looking for next, and learn more broadly about Acuity Insights and the opportunity. 

Conversation with the Manager. You’ll meet our Director of Marketing to dig into the growth work you’ve owned, the decisions you’ve made, and the results. Decision. We bring together feedback from your conversations and typically make a decision within 2–4 business days.

Life at Acuity Insights

We’re a remote-first team of 135+ people, built around trust, flexibility, and giving people meaningful ownership of their work.

Remote-first doesn’t mean working in isolation. We collaborate closely across teams, communicate thoughtfully across time zones, and create intentional opportunities to connect, while protecting the flexibility and focus that make remote work valuable.

Day to day, you can expect:

High trust and autonomy in how you get your work done

Thoughtful, async-friendly communication across a distributed team

Space for focused work alongside intentional collaboration and connection

Colleagues who are generous with their expertise and expect you to bring yours

A sustainable approach to work that values impact over performative busyness

As we grow, we’re deliberate about evolving how we work without adding process for process’s sake. We want people to have the clarity, context, relationships, and room to make good decisions and do work they’re proud of.

About Acuity Insights

Acuity Insights builds products that help higher education institutions make better decisions about people, from admissions through to development.

Our Casper situational judgment test (SJT), created by researchers at McMaster University, has been completed by over 1 million applicants and is one of the most widely used open-response SJTs in higher education, backed by nearly 20 years of research.

Today, we are evolving our products to better connect assessment, insight, and development, helping institutions not just identify potential, but actively support its growth over time. As part of that evolution, we’re increasingly building toward a more connected ecosystem across assessment, education, and learner development. While teams remain focused on their individual products, we’re creating stronger connections across our platform to deliver more cohesive experiences for institutions and learners.

Video Interviews Rater (On-Demand Contract Work Remote in Canada)
Toronto, Canada; Vancouver, Canada; Halifax, Canada; Calgary, Canada; Winnipeg, Canada
Imagine a world where everyone’s full potential is recognized and nurtured.

That’s what we’re building at Acuity Insights.

We believe higher education admissions should look beyond grades and consider the whole person—their experiences, strengths, and unique qualities.

Join a community of Raters helping admissions teams see applicants beyond grades. 

Video Interviews is a fully configurable, asynchronous interview tool designed for higher education admissions teams. It gives programs a scalable way to hear directly from applicants and assess the attributes that matter most to them, without the scheduling, coordination, or workload of live interviews. 

Together with our other products, such as Casper, it helps admissions teams see applicants more fully, beyond grades and test scores, and make confident, defensible decisions about their future professionals. 

As a Video Interviews Rater, you’ll play a critical role in this process. By reviewing and scoring applicant responses, you’ll help our Canadian-based partners make more well-rounded and informed admissions decisions.

This role is designed to fit into your life: 

Work on your own schedule from anywhere in Canada. 

Earn extra income while doing socially meaningful work. 

Join a community of Raters committed to strengthening admissions with reliable, evidence-based assessments. 

What You’ll Do as a Video Interviews Rater

 Become a certified Rater. Complete virtual, scientifically backed, onboarding training to learn how to rate responses of applicants to academic programs.

 Complete ongoing training and mandatory annual recertification. Participate in ongoing refresher training and complete our required paid annual Rater recertification, ensuring your quality of work remains high.

 Rate and score Video Interviews responses : Review applicant video responses and assign scores following scoring guidelines. 

 Share feedback. Provide feedback to help improve and optimize the Video Interviews tool, platforms, and content.

Foundations for Success as a Video Interviews Rater 

 Consistent Engagement & Professionalism—You demonstrate high commitment by consistently participating in rating sessions and upholding a professional demeanour, recognizing the significance of your contribution. 

 Ongoing Skill Development—You regularly engage in the required training and feedback activities to stay informed on best practices and ensure that your evaluations are current and reliable.

 Effective Communication & Responsiveness—You exhibit clear and effective communication, responding promptly to surveys and feedback, and reflecting a proactive and collaborative mindset.

 Empathy & Understanding—You approach every response with empathy and fairness, recognizing the impact your evaluations can have on an applicant’s academic journey.

 Bias Awareness & Integrity—You maintain strong self-awareness, actively reflecting on and addressing potential biases to provide objective and equitable evaluations.

Payments

We issue payments for work you’ve completed via Plooto once a month. 

While there’s no guaranteed minimum work, you can access a quarterly testing schedule, which allows you to choose when to work and estimate potential earnings. Pay may include activities outside of rating, like job training and participating in research studies.

To Qualify as a Video Interviews Rater, you must:

Be a Canadian citizen.

Currently residing in Canada.

Have your own desktop/laptop computer to work on. 

Have no plans to apply to and become a student in a program using an Acuity Insights product (e.g., Video Interviews and Casper) in the next 2-3 years. 

Communicate effectively and proactively in writing, enabling you to raise issues and clearly articulate score choices. 

Demonstrate you have the following soft skills:

Communication

Self-awareness 

Professionalism

Empathy 

We welcome applicants from all walks of life across Canada, which means you’ll also be part of a diverse group of Raters!

Steps to Become a Video Interviews Rater

 Submit Your Application. Complete the online application form. It includes multiple questions to determine if you meet the basic qualifying criteria to become a Video Interviews Rater.

 Take a Mini-Casper and Reading Comprehension Test. If the basic criteria are met, you’ll receive an invitation to take a shortened version of the Casper test. Your responses will be reviewed and rated to determine if you share the four aspects listed in the previous section. You’ll also be required to take a reading comprehension test aimed at evaluating your ability to read and understand written information. This step may take up to 25 minutes to complete.

 Complete Paid Online Rater Training. You will receive an invitation to complete our scientifically backed Rater training, which you must complete within 5 business days. Regardless of the outcome, you will be compensated for your time. 

 Become a Certified Rater. You’ve successfully completed the necessary steps to become a Video Interviews Rater. You’re now certified and can start rating Video Interviews test responses!

How We’ll Train You 

Our Video Interviews Rater training program will equip you with the skills and knowledge needed to make fair, unbiased judgments. 

Throughout the program, you will complete knowledge checks, activities, and exercises that assess and deepen your understanding of the rating process. These interactive elements reinforce learning by enabling you to apply knowledge in realistic scenarios, building confidence and accuracy in your evaluations. 

Before certification, you must complete a calibration assessment and demonstrate consistent alignment with benchmark ratings to ensure your readiness for live assessments.

Video Interviews is a flexible, asynchronous interview tool for higher education admissions. Part of Acuity’s broader admissions offering, it pairs seamlessly with Casper to support a more comprehensive and holistic review process.

With Video Interviews, programs can hear directly from applicants in their own words, without the scheduling challenges of traditional interviews. Applicants complete interviews at their convenience, while admissions teams review responses when it works best for them, saving both time and resources. 

Programs can choose from Acuity’s research-backed questions and rubrics or create their own, ensuring the focus stays on the attributes that matter most. For added support, trained Acuity Raters are available to score responses, helping programs gain meaningful insights without overwhelming internal capacity or adding administrative lift. 

Video Interviews consistently delivers what programs need most: reliable, research-based insights into applicants, with the flexibility to fit seamlessly into existing admissions processes. 

Thanks for considering contributing to Acuity Insights as a Video Interviews Rater!
